title: Ideals in the Zariski characteristic sheaf of a log structure
statement: For a log structure $M$ on a scheme $X$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], restrict its monoid sheaf to Zariski opens and sheafify the quotient by units to obtain $\overline M$. A characteristic ideal is a subsheaf $K\subset\overline M$ stable under multiplication by arbitrary sections. Its stalk consists of germs of its local sections. It is nonempty coherent if locally at each point it is generated as an ideal by a finite positive number of sections. For a specified morphism of sharp sheafed spaces $c:(Y,\overline L)\to(X,\overline M)$, the pulled-back characteristic ideal is the ideal generated sheaf-locally by images of germs in $K$. For a Zariski log structure $M$, the inverse-image log ideal $\pi_M^{-1}K$ consists of log sections whose geometric characteristic germs are represented by Zariski log sections with sharp germ in $K$; classes agree modulo multiplication by units. These constructions use the actual unit-quotient map and sheafification, not a chosen abstract characteristic monoid.
